diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same result can be proved for $\sigma_a^m>\sigma_{bg}^M$, with similar arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (3.1) quotes an inequality valid for Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators, but applies it to Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators. Because the NtD map is monotonically decreasing in conductivity, when $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2$ the operator difference satisfies $\Lambda_{\sigma_1} - \Lambda_{\sigma_2} \le 0$, while the bounds in (3.1) are strictly positive, making (3.1) false. Furthermore, the proof claims the same result holds for $\sigma_a^m > \sigma_{bg}^M$ by symmetric reasoning, but for $\sigma_a > \sigma_{bg}$, the analogous energy identity controls $\int_D (\sigma_a - \sigma_{bg})|\nabla u_D|^2\,dx$, bounding the gradient of the perturbed potential $u_D$ rather than the background potential $u_{bg}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (3.1) with the correct NtD identity $\int_\Omega \sigma_D |\nabla(u_D - u_{bg})|^2\,dx = \langle(\Lambda_{\sigma_D} - \Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}})g, g\rangle - \int_D (\sigma_{bg} - \sigma_a)|\nabla u_{bg}|^2\,dx \ge 0$, which validates the lemma for $\sigma_a^M < \sigma_{bg}^m$, and restrict the scope of the lemma and method to less conductive anomalies $\sigma_a^M < \sigma_{bg}^m$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma 3.1 is invalid as written, and the stated conclusion $\int_D \sigma_{bg}|\nabla u_{bg}|^2\,dx = 0$ is unestablished for more conductive anomalies ($\sigma_a^m > \sigma_{bg}^M$).
issues.title: Invalid NtD energy inequality and unsupported claim for conductive anomalies in Lemma 3.1
issues.why_classification: The correct argument requires replacing the cited DtN inequality with an explicit NtD identity and restricting the advertised scope of the result by excluding the regime $\sigma_a^m > \sigma_{bg}^M$.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (6.1) defines $N$ merely as a bounded operator. If $N$ is not self-adjoint, $\Lambda_n$ is non-self-adjoint, its eigenvalues may be complex (precluding ordering them in decreasing order), and the Weyl perturbation bound $|\tilde{\lambda}_k - \lambda_k| \le \|N\|_2$ does not hold in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the explicit condition that $N$ is a self-adjoint bounded operator.
issues.title: Omitted self-adjointness hypothesis on noise operator in Proposition 6.1
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard assumption that $N$ is self-adjoint is a routine local fix that fully restores the validity of Proposition 6.1 without altering any downstream result or numerical implementation (which already symmetrizes the noise matrix).

issues.failure_explanation: From the upper bound $P - P_b \le \int_D \frac{\sigma_{bg} - \sigma_a}{\sigma_a} \sigma_{bg} |\nabla u_{bg}|^2\,dx$, obtaining a lower bound on $\int_D \sigma_{bg} |\nabla u_{bg}|^2\,dx$ requires dividing by $\sup_{x\in D} \frac{\sigma_{bg}(x) - \sigma_a(x)}{\sigma_a(x)} = \frac{\sigma_{bg}^M - \sigma_a^m}{\sigma_a^m}$. Dividing instead by the infimum $\frac{\Delta_\sigma}{\sigma_a^m} = \frac{\sigma_{bg}^m - \sigma_a^M}{\sigma_a^m}$ reverses the inequality for spatially varying conductivities, making the asserted lower bound in (6.2) mathematically false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\Delta_\sigma$ in the lower bound of (6.2) with $\sigma_{bg}^M - \sigma_a^m$, and adjust the lower endpoint in (6.3) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound in (6.2) does not hold for general inhomogeneous conductivities, and the threshold selection intervals in (6.3) and Remark 6.1 inherit the erroneous factor.
issues.title: Reversed inequality in the lower bound of display (6.2)
issues.why_classification: This is a local algebraic correction that preserves the utility of the bounds; in the piecewise constant conductivity case considered in the examples, $\sigma_{bg}^M - \sigma_a^m$ coincides with $\Delta_\sigma$.
